name: Yi-Kang Hu
occupation: Mayor of Tigard; attorney; small business owner

bio.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Hu lists his occupation as Mayor of Tigard, attorney and small business owner, with a background as a research scientist.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Mayor of Tigard; Attorney; Small Business Owner Occupational Background: Research Scientist

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

bio.statement: The pamphlet lists Hu's prior government experience as Tigard City Council President, Tigard Planning Commission President and the Tigard Transportation Advisory Committee.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Tigard City Council President; Tigard Planning Commission President; Tigard Transportation Advisory Committee

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

bio.statement: The City of Tigard's mayor page describes Hu as a food and drug lawyer who was born in Taiwan, immigrated as a child and previously worked as a research scientist.
bio.excerpt: Mayor Hu is a food & drug lawyer whose practice focuses on FDA law and regulation.

source.publisher: City of Tigard, Mayor Hu page

bio.statement: OPB reported in October 2025 that the Tigard council appointed Hu, then a councilor first elected in 2022, to the mayor's seat in a 5-1 vote.
bio.excerpt: In a 5-1 vote Tuesday night, the council appointed Councilor Yi-Kang Hu to the mayor’s seat

source.publisher: OPB

positions.statement: In his pamphlet statement, Hu says he led efforts to close a $6.5 million budget shortfall while protecting essential services since becoming mayor.
positions.excerpt: led efforts to close a $6.5 million budget shortfall while protecting essential services

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

positions.statement: Hu's pamphlet statement lists affordability as a priority, including controlling costs through responsible budgeting and expanding housing options for every budget and stage of life.
positions.excerpt: Affordability: Control costs for residents through responsible budgeting. Expand housing options for every budget and stage of life.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

positions.statement: Hu's pamphlet statement lists opportunity as a priority: easing business with the city, helping local businesses grow, creating jobs and revitalizing downtown and key commercial districts.
positions.excerpt: Opportunity: Make it easier to do business with the city. Help local businesses and entrepreneurs grow.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

positions.statement: Hu's pamphlet statement lists livability as a priority, including improving transportation safety for pedestrians, cyclists and motorists.
positions.excerpt: Improve transportation safety for pedestrians, cyclists, and motorists.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-35)

positions.statement: Hu's campaign priorities page says safe communities begin with public trust and effective public safety services.
positions.excerpt: Safe communities begin with public trust and effective public safety services.

source.publisher: Yi-Kang Hu campaign website, Priorities

positions.statement: In a May 2026 KATU interview after voters rejected the $150 million bond, Hu said issues with aging, overcrowded and inefficient buildings remain and the city may have to scale projects down or build in phases.
positions.excerpt: We may have to scale them down a little bit or we have to build in phases,

source.publisher: KATU

gaps: No public position found on a specific replacement plan for the police and public works facility beyond May 2026 interview remarks
